description: Construction-site hoarding panel of blue-painted corrugated galvanised sheet on a welded square-tube steel frame with two ground posts.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Construction site fence panel of vertically corrugated galvanised zinc sheet painted pale blue, fixed to a welded square-tube steel frame with a horizontal mid rail, two square steel posts extending below the panel into the ground Materials: Pale blue paint weathered to chalk with the zinc showing through at the ribs, rust streaks from every screw, faded paste-up posters and spray-painted phone numbers near the base.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. 3,906/4,000 triangles, 4/4 draw calls, 3/3 materials, 4/6 unique geometries, three canvases at 3.0 MB, factory ~75 ms. Turntable: 0/180 segment at ~0.43 of frame; 90/270 are UNSEGMENTABLE by size (a 0.13 m sliver, ~2% of frame against the segmenter's 3.5% floor), recorded as a gate limitation of every 3 m panel.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at 3.00 x 2.40 x 0.13 m. The -X post now stands IN the frame plane as the upright, from the ground to 0.10 m above the top rail, and the sheet's wavy top stands 0.06 above the rail -- the plate's top-left corner read off the zoom (post above rail above sheet-top). Rails 50 mm, mid rail at 0.53 of the frame height. Band table residual 0.186 width is the proxy's squarer aspect against the declared 1.25.
featureReviews.notes: The first build put the post BEHIND the sheet with two frame uprights of rail tube; the plate has the post as the upright.

featureReviews.evidence: 40 ribs (20 counted over the 1.5 m of the top-rail zoom) as a sine extrusion at 0.012 amplitude with crest #a4b8c4 / valley #6a8399 vertex tones keyed on the profile itself: the render probes 139-158 across the ribs against the plate's 114 valley / 167 crest. Wavy top edge above the rail at 0 and 315 degrees.
featureReviews.notes: 28 ribs at one flat tone was the first build; a first tone pass at #c8ced0 / #8fa6b8 with gamma 1.6 rendered grey-white at 183 and was re-probed against the plate.

featureReviews.evidence: Frame 6 mm proud of the crests with a mid rail; 60 rusted screw heads at every second crest along all three rails as one InstancedMesh, with rust runs hanging from each rail line in the sheet canvas (bandStreaks at panel-UV v 1.0 / 0.618 / 0.19); rust canvas on the tube at density 110; torn posters and a stencil pane 1.5 x 0.62 at lower left.
featureReviews.notes: Stencil text is a generic bold sans and smaller than the plate's spray; the runs are random along u rather than under each screw.

name: Zinc Sheet Hoarding Panel
nameTh: รั้วสังกะสี
notes: The universal Thai construction fence, seen around every condo site and roadworks compound in runs of dozens. Panels tile edge to edge, so the frame must end flush at both sides. Placement overridden to floor: it stands on its posts, not against a wall. Not breakable. One post per tile: the post is on the -X end and the bay runs to the +X edge, so tiles chain along X with no doubled post at a joint.
